pages.h1: Can Claude check the current gold price?
pages.title: Can Claude check the gold price today? Live per gram
pages.answer: Not from memory. Claude's training data ends at a cutoff date, and the gold price changes every minute, so any number it recalls is old. With web search on, Claude.ai can find a price quoted on a news or dealer page, but that quote may be delayed and Claude still has to do the karat and gram math itself. Connect the free Gold Price per Gram server and Claude reads the spot price from a live feed at the moment you ask, then works out price per gram by karat, in about 160 currencies.
native: Explains karats, troy ounces and melt value correctly.
Does the arithmetic once it has a price you give it.
With web search on, finds a quoted price on a web page.
needs: The spot price right now, from a live feed, with a timestamp.
Price per gram for 10K to 24K and silver, platinum and palladium.
Melt value of a ring or chain from its weight, with a dealer spread.

example.prompt: I have an 18K gold ring that weighs 6.2 g. What is it worth today, and what would a shop that keeps 15% offer?
example.result: 6.2 gram (g) of 18K gold (75% pure) holds 4.65 g of fine gold, a melt value of 584.47 USD at a spot of 3,909.50 USD per troy ounce (as of 2026-11-03T07:58:26Z). With a 15% dealer spread, a buyer would offer about 496.80 USD. Melt value is not a shop price: retail jewellery sells above melt (making charges, design, brand, tax) and buyers pay below it (refining cost and margin). Ask several buyers for their percentage of melt.

faq.q: Is the gold price from the server real time?
faq.a: It reads the spot price from gold-api.com when the tool runs and returns the timestamp with the answer. Currency conversion uses central-bank rates from Frankfurter.

faq.q: Is melt value what a shop will pay?
faq.a: No. Buyers pay below melt to cover refining and margin, and shops sell jewellery above it. The tool lets you set the dealer spread so you can compare offers.

pages.h1: Can Claude check lake levels?
pages.title: Can Claude check lake levels? Live gauge readings
pages.answer: Not on its own. Claude knows what a full pool is and roughly where big reservoirs sat in past years, but not today's reading. Lake levels move every hour, and the numbers sit in USGS, Army Corps, CDEC, Reclamation and Texas Water Development Board gauges that Claude does not read by default. Connect the free Lake Level server and Claude gets the current elevation from the government gauge, the distance below full pool and the change over 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days.
native: Explains full pool, conservation pool and why a lake drops in summer.
Plans a trip around a level you give it.
needs: The current gauge reading for 44 US lakes and reservoirs in 12 states.
Change over 24 hours, 7 days and 30 days, and feet below full pool.
Up to 365 days of daily or weekly history from the same gauge.

example.prompt: Is Lake Travis up or down this week, and how far below full is it?
example.result: Lake Travis (TX) is at 677.09 ft above sea level per the USGS gauge, measured 2026-11-03T01:45:00-06:00. That is 3.91 ft below full pool (681.0 ft). Change: -0.04 ft in 24 h, -0.05 ft in 7 days, -0.72 ft in 30 days.

faq.a: 44 US lakes and reservoirs in 12 states, including Lake Travis, Lake Mead, Lake Powell, Lake Lanier, Lake Texoma and Kentucky Lake. Ask it to search by name or state.

faq.q: Where do the numbers come from?
faq.a: USGS, USACE CWMS, CDEC, Reclamation RISE and TWDB gauges, read at call time. Each answer names the gauge and links to its data page.

pages.h1: Can Claude calculate the no tax on overtime deduction?
pages.title: Can Claude calculate no tax on overtime? Schedule 1-A
pages.query: can claude calculate no tax on overtime
pages.answer: Only if its training includes the July 2025 law, and many Claude versions were trained before it or know it only in outline. The deduction has a $12,500 cap ($25,000 joint), a MAGI phase-out from $150,000 and a rule that only the half-time premium counts, which is easy to get wrong in a long answer. Connect the free No Tax on Overtime server and Claude works out the qualified overtime, the cap and the phase-out the way Schedule 1-A does, for 2025 to 2028.
native: Explains in general terms what the overtime deduction is.
Does simple sums when you give it the qualified amount.
needs: The P.L. 119-21 rules: caps, MAGI phase-outs and the FLSA premium rule.
Tips and senior deductions with the same rules.
The 2025 and 2026 IRS brackets to estimate the tax you save.

example.prompt: I am single, MAGI $68,000. I worked 300 overtime hours in 2025 at $24 an hour, time and a half. What is my overtime deduction?
example.result: Qualified overtime premium $3,600. After the $12,500 cap: $3,600. MAGI $68,000 is not above the $150,000 threshold, so there is no phase-out. Deduction for 2025: $3,600. Only the FLSA premium (the "half" in time-and-a-half) qualifies, not the straight-time part or any extra premium.

faq.q: Does the whole overtime check count?
faq.a: No. Only the premium part counts, the extra half in time and a half. In the example, $10,800 of overtime pay gives a $3,600 deduction.

faq.q: Does it lower Social Security and Medicare tax?
faq.a: No. It lowers federal income tax only. Payroll taxes still apply to overtime pay.

pages.h1: Can Claude adjust a price for inflation?
pages.title: Can Claude adjust for inflation? Official CPI data
pages.answer: It can do the formula, but it does not know the latest CPI. The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes a new index every month, and Claude only knows the months before its training cutoff, so an inflation-adjusted figure it gives from memory is stale or guessed. Connect the free CPI Inflation Calculator server and Claude uses official BLS CPI-U, CPI-W and core CPI values from 1913 to the latest month, then gives the exact adjusted amount and the yearly rate.
native: Knows the inflation formula: amount times new CPI over old CPI.
Explains the difference between CPI-U, CPI-W and core CPI.
needs: Official monthly and yearly CPI values, 1913 to the latest release.
Whether a raise beat inflation over the same months.
The Social Security COLA for a given year.

example.prompt: What is $50,000 from January 2015 worth now, in buying power?
example.result: $50,000.00 in January 2015 has the same buying power as $72,085.99 in September 2026 (CPI-U 233.707 to 336.94). Cumulative inflation 44.17%, about 3.19% a year over 11.67 years.
example.note: On this run the live BLS check hit its daily request limit, so the server used its bundled BLS data through September 2026 and said so in the answer.

faq.a: CPI-U, all items, US city average, not seasonally adjusted, unless you ask for CPI-W or core CPI.

faq.q: What if the newest month is missing?
faq.a: The answer names the latest month it used. When the live BLS API is not reachable it falls back to bundled data and says so.

pages.h1: Can Claude count business days?
pages.title: Can Claude count business days between two dates?
pages.answer: It often gets them wrong. Counting business days means walking a calendar day by day, skipping weekends and the federal holidays, including observed days when a holiday falls on a weekend, and language models are weak at that kind of exact date walk over weeks or months. Connect the free US Federal Holidays and Business Days server and Claude gets an exact count from the OPM rules, 1971 to 2100, plus due dates that roll past weekends and holidays.

example.result: There are 32 business days from 2026-12-01 to 2027-01-15 (start included, end included) on the federal calendar: 46 calendar days, 12 weekend days. Excluded weekday holidays: 2026-12-25 Christmas Day; 2027-01-01 New Year's Day.

pages.h1: Can Claude calculate DSCR for a rental loan?
pages.title: Can Claude calculate DSCR for a rental property loan?
pages.answer: Yes, if you give it every number, but the loan payment math is where long answers slip. DSCR is qualifying rent divided by the full monthly housing cost, and that cost needs an exact amortized payment plus tax, insurance and HOA. Claude also can't know which vacancy factor or ratio band your lender uses. Connect the free DSCR Loan Calculator server and Claude gets the exact payment, PITIA and ratio, the largest loan a target DSCR allows, and the rent you'd need.
native: Explains DSCR, PITIA and why lenders want 1.0 or 1.25.
Gets a close answer when you supply the monthly payment yourself.
needs: The exact principal and interest payment for any rate and term, or interest only.
The maximum loan for a target DSCR and LTV, and the rent needed to hit it.
Side by side scenarios for down payment and rate.

example.prompt: A rental rents for $2,400 a month. I buy it for $300,000 with 25% down at 7.25% for 30 years. Tax is $3,600 a year and insurance $1,500. What is the DSCR with 5% vacancy?
example.result: A $225,000.00 loan at 7.25% over 30 years has a monthly payment of $1,534.90 and PITIA of $1,959.90. Qualifying rent of $2,280.00 gives a DSCR of 1.16 (exact 1.163325), in the 1.00 to 1.24 band. Rent covers PITIA. Many DSCR programs accept 1.00 or more; lenders that want 1.25 will not.

faq.q: Is 1.16 good enough for a DSCR loan?
faq.a: Many programs accept 1.00 or more, and some want 1.25. Minimums and pricing differ by lender, so the server labels the band and doesn't approve anything.

faq.q: Does it use current mortgage rates?
faq.a: No. You give it the rate your lender quoted. It doesn't fetch market rates.
